subject: Pricing guardrails & minimums - order form redlines
messages:
From: Tom Brooks <procurement@acme-corp.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Lara Chen <finance@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing guardrails and minimum commitments - initial redlines

Rachel / team,

Appreciate the demo last week. Our procurement team reviewed the draft order form and attached a redline (Acme_OrderForm_Redlines_v1.docx). High level asks from Acme: 

- Remove the hard minimum monthly spend. We can negotiate an annual committed spend instead, but we want flexibility on months when usage is unexpectedly low.
- Limit the vendor's unilateral price increase ability and add a 30-day notice + customer remedy period.
- Cap overage exposure: we cannot accept open-ended per-token overage beyond 150% of committed monthly baseline without a negotiated cap.
- Simplify true-up mechanics and set a quarterly true-up cadence.

Please review and send a counterproposal. Our legal also flagged Exhibit C language around "floor" and "cap" as too punitive; procurement would prefer guardrails that protect both parties. We need the final order form for our CFO by 11/18.

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_Redlines_v1.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Tom Brooks
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Corp
procurement@acme-corp.com

From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing guardrails and minimum commitments - initial redlines

Looping you both in on Acme's redlines. Quick thoughts before I reply to Tom: 

- Sales: we can offer a 12-month committed ARR with quarterly true-ups instead of an unbending monthly floor. In exchange, propose a 10% introductory credit on the first quarter to ease adoption. Marissa, please draft the commercial concession matrix (tiers, effective discount, and early-exit pro-rata).
- Legal: Karthik, Acme wants an overage cap around 150% of baseline but they phrased it badly. We should propose a protective overage cap linked to committed spend (e.g., overages capped at X% of committed quarterly spend) and keep audit/usage review windows. Also need to tighten the vendor price-adjustment notice window.

Goal: a cleaned order form + simple Exhibit C markup that preserves our economics but addresses Acme's flexibility ask. Can you both turn around something by EOD tomorrow so I can send a formal counter?

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 14:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing guardrails and minimum commitments - initial redlines

Rachel / Marissa,

Attached are legal's suggested edits and a short rationale (see pricing-exhibit-markup.pdf). Key redline proposals below: 

1) Commitments: Replace "minimum monthly commitment" with a "Committed Annual Spend (CAS)" concept. CAS is expressed as an annual dollar commitment with quarterly true-ups and a reconciliation. If quarterly usage < prorated CAS, customer owes the difference for that quarter (true-up), unless usage shortfall is driven by Force Majeure or agreed product outages.

2) Floor flexibility: Add a "temporary reduction" clause allowing one 30-day reduction window per 12-month period (requires written notice 14 days prior). This addresses Acme's flexibility ask while preserving predictability for capacity planning.

3) Overage cap: Propose a capped overage model: default cap = 125% of the customer's committed quarterly baseline in $ terms; any demand beyond that triggers an automatic temporary rate increase band (not to exceed X% above standard overage rate) and a capacity review. This protects Redwood from runaway tails while giving Acme certainty.

4) Price changes and notice: Require minimum 60 days' notice for material price increases and provide a customer remedy period (30 days) during which customer may terminate for convenience with pro-rata refund of unused committed spend.

5) Audits & data retention: Clarify audit windows (annual, 30-day notice) and specify token-level usage granularity for true-ups.

I've drafted markup for Exhibit C and a short paragraph for the order form that implements CAS + quarterly true-ups + one temporary reduction window. I've kept language negotiable on the exact % caps — suggest we propose 125% and be prepared to move to 150% for strategic deals.

Next steps: Marissa, incorporate a commercial table showing (A) 12-mo CAS, (B) Tiered unit pricing, (C) Intro credit for Q1, (D) overage cap % and corresponding rate bands. Once we have a combined doc, Rachel can send to Acme with a short note.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
To: Tom Brooks <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Lara Chen <finance@acme-corp.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposed counter: CAS + quarterly true-ups + introductory credit (attached)

Tom / Lara,

Thanks for the redlines — appreciate the clarity. Attached is our proposed order form that tries to balance Acme's need for flexibility with Redwood's operating predictability (RWD-Proposed-OrderForm-Nov2025.docx). High level: 

- Committed Annual Spend (CAS): 12-month commitment with quarterly true-ups and reconciliation.
- Temporary reduction: one 30-day reduction window per 12 months with 14 days' notice.
- Overage cap: default cap at 125% of committed quarterly baseline in $ terms; higher caps are available for expanded commitments.
- Introductory commercial concession: 10% credit applied to consumption charges in Q1 after go-live.
- Price changes: 60-day notice and 30-day remedy/terminate option with pro-rata refund.

We believe this addresses Acme's flexibility ask while keeping pricing guardrails reasonable for both sides. If you prefer a different overage cap (e.g., 150%), we can show the economics side-by-side quickly.

Attached: RWD-Proposed-OrderForm-Nov2025.docx (docx), pricing-exhibit-markup.pdf (pdf)
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/some-envelope-id

Can you confirm whether the CFO would accept CAS + quarterly true-ups by 11/18? If useful, we can schedule a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk the changes.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Phone: (415) 555-0192

From: Tom Brooks <procurement@acme-corp.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Lara Chen <finance@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed counter: CAS + quarterly true-ups + introductory credit (attached)

Rachel,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear proposal. A few comments from Acme finance / procurement after a brief review: 

- CAS + quarterly true-ups is acceptable in principle. CFO prefers the option of a 6-month ramp rather than full CAS if we can phase in the committed baseline for the first two quarters. Is Redwood open to a phased CAS where Q1 counts at 50% toward annual CAS, Q2 at 75%, then full CAS thereafter?
- The 125% overage cap is close, but finance would feel better with a 135% floor cap or a stepped cap (125% for Q1 onboarding, 135% thereafter). Can we show both options with the economics?
- Regarding termination remedy: we cannot accept a pro-rata refund of unused committed spend; finance prefers an offset model where unused committed credits roll into the next quarter for up to two quarters.

We'll schedule an internal review with CFO on 11/13. If Redwood can send a version reflecting the phased ramp and the stepped cap options, that would speed approval. Also please include a short example calculation for clarity in the order form (one paragraph).

Attachments: none

Tom Brooks
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Corp
procurement@acme-corp.com
thread_summary: Negotiation over pricing guardrails for Acme: customer submitted redlines wanting removal of strict monthly floors; Redwood proposed Committed Annual Spend with quarterly true-ups, one temporary reduction window, and a default 125% overage cap plus a 10% Q1 credit. Acme countered preferring a phased ramp and stepped overage caps and requested credit-roll mechanics instead of pro-rata refunds. Action: Redwood to produce revised order form with phased ramp and stepped-cap economics for CFO review by 11/18.
